message: Consistency claim at the edges→CSR data-flow seam invites the wrong inference: 'MVCC de graça' is true of the theodb.graph_csr catalog row, but traversal results (graph_expand/graph_ppr/graph_rag_search) are served from the CSR frozen at graph_build/graph_refold time — committed edge INSERTs after the build are silently invisible to every traversal until an explicit graph_refold, with no staleness signal (the per-backend cache keyed by built_at, graph.rs:17-20, only invalidates on refold — it never detects new edges). The lakehouse doc handles the analogous seam with an explicit freshness contract (theodb.htap_freshness); this doc offers refold (§4) but never states the silent-staleness failure mode.
evidence: WAL-logged, crash-safe e MVCC de graça pelo próprio PostgreSQL
remediation: Add an operational note: traversal reflects the CSR as of the last graph_build/graph_refold — new committed edges are invisible until refold; there is no freshness function, so schedule refold after ingest.

message: 20 `graph*.rs:NNN` line-number references spread across nearly every section ('Verificado em ...:NNN' after each function), including a range pin `graph.rs:334-493`, versus the 0-2 header-only convention of docs/features/01-12. Each pin is a rot site invalidated by any edit above it in the file; with no verified-at commit marker the doc cannot signal staleness (rot-resistance principle: reference stable symbols, not line offsets).
remediation: Confine line pins to the Status header and reference functions by symbol name (`graph_build` em `graph.rs`) in section bodies.

message: SSoT violation: the extension boundary is stated inconsistently across the doc set. Docs 13:31, 14:37, 17:34 and 19:33 attribute catalogs/AMs/functions directly to the extension 'theodb' ('Instala a extensão theodb (own-code), que provê...'), while docs 15:30 and 16:31 correctly state the two-extension layering ('Instala a extensão theodb e sua base theodb_rs via CASCADE'). The repo's actual layout confirms the latter: theodb.control declares requires = 'theodb_rs', and every cited symbol (#[pg_extern] in theodb_rs/src/graph.rs, am/mod.rs, etc.) belongs to the base extension theodb_rs, not to the SQL wrapper extension theodb. The same architectural fact restated in two divergent formulations across 7 sibling docs is a divergence bomb: a reader debugging '\dx' output or a DROP EXTENSION cascade gets two different mental models depending on which page they read.
evidence: Instala a extensão `theodb` (own-code), que provê os catálogos `theodb.graph_csr` / `theodb.graph_nodes` / `theodb.graph_edges` e todas as funções `theodb.graph_*` ... [vs 15-lakehouse-parquet.md:30] Instala a extensão `theodb` e sua base `theodb_rs` via `CASCADE` [vs theodb.control] requires = 'theodb_rs'
remediation: Standardize the section-1 boilerplate across all 7 docs on the accurate two-extension formulation used by docs 15/16 (theodb + base theodb_rs via CASCADE).

message: 15 file:line references through the body (kind numbers pinned to columnar_agg.rs lines: `:328`, `:352-360`, `:362-371`, `:374-378`, `:306`, plus guc.rs and arrow_cache.rs pins), versus the 0-2 header-only convention of docs 01-12. The admission-kind line pins in particular sit in a hot file (columnar_agg.rs) where any refactor shifts every offset — 15 independent drift sites with no verified-at anchor.
remediation: Reference the admission guard by symbol/section, keep line pins only in the Status header.

message: Missing scaling/deployment limit at the I/O seam: the doc announces removal of the 'último componente C++/httpfs' but never states the consequence — the own-code Parquet path reads/writes the server-local filesystem only (theodb_rs/src/parquet.rs:60: object_store LocalFileSystem). A 'lakehouse' surface is normally expected to reach object storage (s3://, gs://); after the httpfs removal there is no remote-path support, and every example silently assumes a local server path. Operators planning object-store lakehouses need this limit documented (honest-limits principle).
evidence: Rust (DataFusion + Arrow, Apache-2.0) — **sem DuckDB** (o `pg_duckdb`, último componente C++/httpfs do projeto, foi **removido por completo** no M143)
remediation: State explicitly that v1 Parquet I/O is server-local filesystem only (LocalFileSystem, parquet.rs:60) — no s3:// or object-store paths — and mark remote object-store support as follow-on.

message: Two consecutive status blockquotes both declaring '✅ Entregue' (lines 3-11 and 13-17), duplicating the delivery claim and repeating the same benchmark citation (`parquet-reader-owncode-spike.md` linked in both blocks). Docs 01-12 use a single `> **Status:**` block; a future status change (e.g. write-type expansion) now requires two synchronized edits in the same header, and the two blocks can drift apart.
remediation: Merge the two blockquotes into the single Status block used by docs 01-12.

message: Densest file:line coupling of the new doc set: 27 `theodb_rs/src/*.rs:NNN` references scattered through every section body, versus the established convention in docs/features/01-12 of 0-2 refs confined to the Status header (e.g. 02-indice-hnsw.md has 1, 01 has 0). Line numbers rot on any edit to vectorizer.rs/guc.rs, and the doc pins volatile runtime constants to them too (batch=10/lease=120s/5 tentativas at line 65-66, dead-letter default 1000 at 212). There is no 'verified at commit/version' anchor anywhere, so a reader cannot tell whether the 27 pins are still valid — each is an independent silent-drift site (single-source-of-truth violation: the code is the SSoT, the doc re-states it 27 times).
remediation: Keep file:line pins only in the Status header (per 01-12 convention), demote body refs to path-or-symbol level, and add a single 'verificado em <tag/commit>' marker so rot is detectable.

message: The measured verdict '2,6–3,9× mais rápido' is hard-coded 3 times in one doc (lines 14, 126-127, 176), and the FastScan gain '1,07–1,22×' twice (16, 110). The SSoT is the benchmark artifact (`e2-symqg-inpg-verdict.md`); every in-prose repetition is a drift site when the verdict is re-measured (e.g. after a scan optimization) — one re-measurement then requires 3+ synchronized edits or the doc self-contradicts.
evidence: Para produção vetorial, o `theodb_hnsw` é o caminho recomendado: medido **2,6–3,9× mais rápido** que o `theodb_symqg` in-PG no recall casado em SIFT1M
remediation: State the number once (Status header) and have body sections point to the header/benchmark artifact instead of restating it.

message: The volatile shipping-status banner '⚠️ API-alvo / não-shipped no binário default (requer --features spike-lexical...)' is repeated verbatim in 6 sections (3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 11) plus 2 pg_textsearch variants (8, 9). The established convention (06-busca-hibrida.md) consolidates non-shipped surface in ONE '🎯 API-alvo / roadmap (não-shipped)' footer section. If/when the feature enters the default binary (an explicitly anticipated follow-up), 6-8 scattered banners must be edited in lockstep — each a stale-status drift site.
evidence: > ⚠️ **API-alvo / não-shipped no binário default** (requer `--features spike-lexical`, ver seção 3).
remediation: Declare the shipping status once (Status header already does) and mark per-section applicability with a short cross-reference to that single source.

message: The reloption reference table wholesale duplicates code constants — 10 rows each restating type/default/range from options.rs AND carrying two line-number pins per row (definition + registration, ~20 line refs in one table). Any change to options.rs (new option, range bump, reordered registration) silently drifts the table: defaults/ranges have no oracle and the line pins rot on the next edit. This is the single largest duplicated-knowledge surface in the diff (SSoT: options.rs is authoritative; the table is a hand-maintained copy with no verified-at anchor).
evidence: | `lists` | int | `100` | `1 … 32768` | Nº de listas k-means do `theodb_ivfflat` (parâmetro de build). | `options.rs:15-17` · reg. `112-120` |
remediation: Drop the per-row line pins (cite `theodb_rs/src/am/options.rs` once) and add a 'verificado em <tag/commit>' marker on the table — or generate/verify the table from options.rs in CI.

message: Measured numbers are each hard-coded 3-4 times within the doc: RaBitQ '3.28× menor' at lines 13, 210-211, 316, 329; 'cold 2.5–2.8×' at 211, 316, 329-330; SQ8 '3.5×' at 15, 187, 315, 329-330. The SSoT is the benchmark artifact; a re-measurement (new hardware, new dataset scale) requires 3-4 synchronized edits per number or the doc becomes internally inconsistent.
evidence: | RaBitQ f32-free (v8) | `+ refine=2, rabitq_bits=7` | 3.28× menor (medido) | paridade (−1.1..1.6 pp) | warm sem ganho / cold 2.5–2.8× (E1) | ivfflat |
remediation: Keep measured numbers in one place (header or trade-off table) and reference them from the other sections.
